invariant: The error helper validates protected failures; checksyntax constructs Unicode escape source, compiles it and requires the actual result to equal the original byte string. Empty/outside offset requests return nil as specified.

For each invoked sequence, len, char, codepoint, offset start/end positions, forward/backward iteration, charpattern and generated Unicode escape source agree. Every continuation byte and all substring boundaries are exercised.
utf8.len returns nil and the exact first invalid byte for truncated, oversized and spurious continuation sequences.
utf8.codes reports malformed/out-of-range strings, and its exposed iterator handles empty strings and invalid starting positions without a fabricated element.
Offset bounds and continuation-byte starting positions raise the expected errors; len rejects invalid bounds, while incomplete codepoint offset queries report available byte endpoints.
ASCII and Chinese strings pass the full checker. codepoint ranges reject malformed tails/outside bounds and handle empty ranges; lax surrogate and largest supported codepoints remain explicit.
char supports no arguments, embedded zeros and the largest lax codepoint, rejects negative/oversized values, and strict codepoint/len reject surrogates, overlong sequences and invalid bytes.
Empty input and every minimum/maximum sequence size pass all checker APIs. Lax five/six-byte encodings produce their actual extended codepoints and source escape byte lengths.
